title: artifact@1 — Munarium Datastore identity rules
description: Not a message shape: the machine-readable specification of how the three canonical documents are encoded before hashing, so that `index_version_id` and `artifact_id` mean the same thing in every implementation. A document conforming to this schema DESCRIBES a canonicalization version; the rules are the `const` values below, which is what makes a drift in an implementation a test failure rather than a discussion. This is deliberately NOT `canon@1` (matrix/contract/canonicalization.schema.json): that one canonicalizes a tabular RESULT for evidence identity, this one canonicalizes a JSON DOCUMENT for artifact identity. Two different problems; conflating them under one name would be worse than having two.

encoding.description: RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme, restricted. JCS is chosen rather than invented because an independently specified scheme with third-party test vectors is auditable in a way a house format is not.

key_order.const: object members sorted by UTF-16 code unit, ascending

whitespace.const: none: no space after ':' or ',', no newlines, no trailing newline

string_escaping.const: minimal per RFC 8785: only " \ and C0 controls are escaped; \b \f \n \r \t use their short forms, other controls use \u00XX lowercase hex

unicode.const: no normalization: the UTF-8 bytes of a string are hashed as given, exactly as canon@1 also refuses to normalize

value_types.description: The closed set of JSON value types a canonical document may contain. Floating-point numbers are FORBIDDEN, which is the one place this profile is stricter than JCS.

const: number with a fractional part or exponent

why_no_floats.const: JCS number canonicalization is ES6 Number::toString, and it is the part implementations get wrong -- shortest round-trip formatting, exponent thresholds, negative zero. Nothing in a BuildSpec, a plan or a manifest needs a float: dimensions, byte lengths, counts and positions are integers, and a genuine ratio is carried as a decimal STRING at a declared scale, the same discipline canon@1 applies to its decimal type. A rule that removes a whole class of implementation divergence is worth more than the convenience it costs.

integer_range.const: signed 64-bit; a value outside it is refused rather than truncated or widened to a float

decimal_as_string.const: base-10 at a declared scale, always with that many fraction digits, optional leading '-', no exponent, no thousands separators -- identical to canon@1's decimal encoding so one reading of 'exact decimal' serves both

input.const: the canonical UTF-8 bytes as defined above, with nothing appended -- no trailing newline, no length prefix, no domain separator

index_version_id.const: 'idx2-' followed by the full 64-hex SHA-256 of the canonical BuildSpec document. The BuildSpec already carries the logical scope and the source snapshot, so nothing is concatenated outside the document -- a concatenation is a second format to get wrong.

artifact_id.const: the full 64-hex SHA-256 of the canonical manifest.json bytes, with no prefix. There is exactly ONE physical content identifier; a second physical hash must not be introduced.

artifact_plan_sha256.const: the full 64-hex SHA-256 of the canonical ArtifactBuildPlan document; recorded in the manifest and in the catalog, and the single-flight key for a build attempt

legacy_ids.const: existing 'idx-' identifiers are NOT recomputed under these rules and are not retroactively changed; a mirror artifact reuses the PostgreSQL index_version_id verbatim

manifest_is_content_pure.const: the manifest contains no build timestamp, builder identity, attempt id, hostname, or any other non-content metadata. Those live in the catalog row and the attempt row. This is what makes a byte-identical rebuild converge on one artifact_id instead of colliding.

spec_excludes_physical.const: the BuildSpec excludes the selected engine, crate revision, artifact envelope format, graph/quantization parameters, thread counts, build timestamp and query-only fusion knobs -- so an engine upgrade changes artifact_id alone and never invalidates a session's logical pin

invariant.const: changing a build timestamp, builder or attempt changes NEITHER id; changing an engine or envelope format changes artifact_id ONLY; changing a source, chunker, extractor, analyzer contract or embedder changes the logical index_version_id
